sources.title: Michael W. Davis, The Geometry and Topology of Coxeter Groups (first-edition author manuscript, 2007-2008)
sources.locator: Chapter 4, printed pp. 46-47 (Lemma 4.2.2, Lemma 4.2.3) and pp. 55-56 (Remarks 4.8.1-4.8.2, Tits' Lemma 4.8.3 with the inductive scheme (P_n),(Q_n)); Chapter 6, printed pp. 90-91 (Lemma 6.6.8 with proof); Appendix D.1, printed pp. 440-441 (the half-space sets A_s and Lemma D.1.5, Cases 1 and 2); Appendix D.2, printed pp. 442-445 (Examples D.2.1, Lemmas D.2.2-D.2.5, Corollaries D.2.4, Theorems D.2.6-D.2.8 and Corollary D.2.9).

contents.name: Lemma D.1.5, Case 1 (m=infinity): the dual basis formulas s.xi=-xi+2phi, t.xi=xi, s.phi=phi, t.phi=2xi-phi and the identification of the W_{s,t}-action on the affine line with the standard action of the infinite dihedral group on E^1
Lemma D.1.5, Case 2 (m finite): the m root lines cut the plane into 2m chambers that are the sectors of the dihedral group W_{s,t} of order 2m, and C is one of them
Examples D.2.1(i): the infinite dihedral Tits cone, with C^f=C-{0}, and the descriptions of U and I in coordinates x1=e1(x), x2=e2(x)
Examples D.2.1(ii): hyperbolic triangle groups, where U is the positive light cone and I its interior
contents.reason: No claim of this pair treats Lorentzian signature, hyperbolic reflection groups or light cones; the examples of this page are the infinite dihedral, A_2 and product types only, so the hyperbolic illustration is not built here.

contents.name: Lemma D.2.2: the chambers C and wC lie on opposite sides of the hyperplane E*_s fixed by rho*(s) if and only if l(w) > l(sw)
Lemma D.2.3: for y in the negative open chamber, y lies in U if and only if W is finite
Corollary D.2.4: the origin of E* lies in the interior of U if and only if W is finite
Lemma D.2.5: if x,y in C and w in W satisfy wx=y, then x=y and w lies in W_{S(x)}
Theorem D.2.6(i): the natural map from the basic construction U(W,C) to U is a bijection whose fibres are the sets W_{S(x)}
Theorem D.2.6(ii)-(iii): the restriction U(W,C^f) to I is a W-equivariant homeomorphism and I is the interior of U
Theorem D.2.7(i): U is convex
Theorem D.2.7(ii): every closed line segment in U meets only finitely many face cells w C_T
contents.reason: The finite face-crossing count along a segment is not used by any item of this pair: convexity is proved here through the finite-negativity criterion, and no later claim of these two pages consumes the crossing refinement.

contents.name: Theorem D.2.8 and Corollary D.2.9: I is a model for the universal space EW, W acts properly on I, and finite subgroups of W lie in spherical parabolics
contents.reason: The finite-subgroup containment clause is proved at thm-cg-finite-subgroups-lie-in-spherical-parabolics using the Davis CAT(0) circumcenter and cell-isotropy route. Proper action on the Davis complex is thm-cg-davis-complex-cell-incidence-and-stabilizers (3). Neither an EW universal-space theorem nor properness of the action on the Tits-cone interior I is asserted by this selected pair; the grouped source statements do not add those promises.

contents.name: Theorem D.2.10: the centre of an infinite irreducible Coxeter group is trivial
contents.reason: The centre computation is stated by Davis as an application of the basic construction to the interior of the Tits cone; no item of this pair makes a group-theoretic centre claim, and the argument needs the proper action recorded above.

contents.name: Lemma 6.6.8 with its proof: for x,y in a fundamental chamber C of a finite reflection group with wx=y, one has x=y and w in W_{S(x)} (the argument Davis reuses for Lemma D.2.5)
Lemma 4.2.2: a reflection r belongs to R(1,w) if and only if l(w) > l(rw) (the reflection-crossing criterion for the Cayley graph)
Lemma 4.2.3: every reflection of a special subgroup W_T is conjugate inside W_T to an element of T
contents.reason: This pair needs no normal form for reflections of special subgroups: the reflection/root dictionary and parabolic factorisation are supplied by the sibling canonical-roots and parabolic pages, which this page cites as items rather than re-deriving.

contents.name: Remark 4.8.1 and Tits' Lemma 4.8.3 with the inductive scheme (P_n),(Q_n) proving property (P) from its rank-two cases
contents.reason: Tits' pre-fundamental-set lemma with its simultaneous (P_n),(Q_n) induction is formalised locally as lem-cg-rank-two-prefix-and-chamber-length-induction on the sibling page, which is this page's declared prerequisite; this pair consumes its chamber-side consequences only, through the root-length criterion and the sign of the simple coordinate.

sources.title: Nicolas Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody groups and Lie algebras (lecture notes, November 9, 2015)
sources.locator: Chapter 6, Section 6.5 'Dominant chambers and Tits cone', printed pp. 55-56: Definition 6.5.1 and Theorem 6.5.2 (i)-(vi) with its complete proof.

contents.name: Definition 6.5.1: the dominant chamber C_R={h in h_R : <h,alpha_i> >= 0} and the Tits cone X = union over w of wC_R
Theorem 6.5.2(i): for lambda in C_R the isotropy group W_lambda is generated by the simple reflections it contains
Theorem 6.5.2(ii): the dominant chamber C_R is a fundamental domain for the action of W on X, with the reduced-expression proof
Theorem 6.5.2(iii): X={lambda : <lambda,alpha> < 0 for a finite number of alpha in Delta_+}, and X is a convex cone, with the finite-set descent proof
Theorem 6.5.2(iv): C_R={h : h-w(h)=sum c_i alpha_i^vee with c_i >= 0 for all w}, with its induction on l(w)
contents.reason: The coroot-difference characterisation of the dominant chamber is not needed here: this pair describes the chamber by the collision and stabilizer theorems, and uses no coroot or Weyl-vector argument, so the clause is deliberately not built.

contents.name: Theorem 6.5.2(v): the equivalences |W| finite, X=h_R, |Delta| finite and |Delta^vee| finite
contents.reason: The finiteness criterion for Coxeter groups is the central theorem of the later finite-classification page, which the plan orders after this pair; this page proves only the interior criterion for a single functional, not the global equivalence.

contents.name: Theorem 6.5.2(vi): the orbit W.h is finite if and only if h lies in the interior of X, with the neighbourhood argument using the finitely many roots Delta^h_+
